subject: physics
question_text: A thermos flask containing a liquid is shaken vigorously. What happens to the temperature of the liquid?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 13 (printed p.125). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: an insulated thermos flask has ΔQ = 0; shaking does work on the liquid, so the work done BY the liquid, W, is negative, and the first law ΔU = ΔQ − W = −W is then positive, so the internal energy and temperature of the liquid rise.

steps.margin_note: ΔQ = 0 and W < 0 together are the first mark.
steps.why: The first law needs both facts together — no heat crosses the insulated wall, and the work is done on the liquid, not by it — before the sign of ΔU can be found.
common_mistakes: Saying heat is added by the shaking. Shaking does mechanical work; it exchanges no heat through the insulated wall.
Taking W as positive. Work done ON the liquid makes W, the work done BY the liquid, negative.
steps.memory_tip: Insulated flask: ΔQ = 0 always. Shaking: work done ON the liquid, so W is negative.

steps.margin_note: ΔU = −W > 0, and the stated conclusion that the temperature rises, are the second mark.
steps.why: Internal energy is the only place the work done on an insulated liquid can go, and a rise in internal energy of a liquid shows up as a rise in its temperature.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔU = ΔQ + W with the wrong sign convention and reaching the wrong sign for ΔU.
Stopping at 'internal energy increases' without saying the temperature rises — that is the actual answer to the question asked.
steps.memory_tip: ΔQ = 0 and W negative together make ΔU positive: the liquid warms up.

insider_note: The temperature rises, not falls — work is done ON the liquid by the shaking, so ΔU is positive despite there being no heat supplied.
